proof.text: The chosen compactification makes the structure morphism $a$ a compactifiable morphism between Noetherian schemes: $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian and a finite-type scheme over it is Noetherian. The constant finite coefficient object $A_{n,X}$ is in $D^b_{ctf}$ on both the etale and the pro-etale site, so [thm-fix-general-biduality], which is stated on either site, applies to it there. Its image under the duality anti-equivalence is $R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(A_{n,X},\omega)\simeq\omega$ for the dualizing object of that site; hence $\omega_{X,\mathrm{et}}=a^\times A_n$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$ and $\omega_{X,n}=Ra_n^!A_n$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$. Together with the given finite-Tor hypotheses on $M$, this supplies the coefficient-domain hypotheses needed below.

proof.text: By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], choose a bounded constructible etale complex $M_{\mathrm{et}}$ and an isomorphism $\nu_X^*M_{\mathrm{et}}\cong M$. Since $M$ is finite-Tor and has this etale origin, clause (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] verifies that $M_{\mathrm{et}}$ has finite Tor amplitude on the etale site. Thus $M_{\mathrm{et}}\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$. Apply [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] with first input $M_{\mathrm{et}}$ and second input $\omega_{X,\mathrm{et}}=a^\times A_n$. It identifies the pullback of the etale internal Hom with $R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(M,\omega_{X,n})$, identifies $\nu_X^*\omega_{X,\mathrm{et}}$ with $\omega_{X,n}$, and preserves the evaluation pairing.

proof.text:
The finite-Tor direct-image stability statement [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images], clause (3), puts $F_nM=Ra_{!,n}M$ in $D^b_{ctf}(s,A_n)$ on the pro-etale site. The compact-support comparison [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] gives a witness $F_nM\simeq
u_s^*(Ra^{\mathrm{Et}}_!M_{\mathrm{et}})$. The etale object $Ra^{\mathrm{Et}}_!M_{\mathrm{et}}$ is bounded below. It is bounded constructible: by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] (ii) the bounded constructible object $F_nM$ is $
u_s^*G$ for some $G\in D^b_c(s_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$, and since $
u_s^*$ is fully faithful on bounded-below derived categories [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], the isomorphism $
u_s^*G\cong
u_s^*(Ra^{\mathrm{Et}}_!M_{\mathrm{et}})$ comes from an isomorphism $G\cong Ra^{\mathrm{Et}}_!M_{\mathrm{et}}$. Applying clause (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] to this witness also verifies the finite-Tor hypothesis for the etale compact-support object, so $Ra^{\mathrm{Et}}_!M_{\mathrm{et}}\in D^b_{ctf}(s_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$, as needed for the site comparison at $s$ in Step 4. Therefore the point node [lem-coef-finite-point-internal-hom-evaluation] applies to $C=F_nM$, and with $\operatorname{Fib}_s(F_nM)=C_n(M)$ it supplies the evaluation-defined point comparison to $R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(C_n(M),A_n)$.

proof.text:
Apply [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] to the compactifiable etale map $a$, the complex $M_{\mathrm{et}}$, and $K=A_{n,s}$. It gives
$$Ra_*R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(M_{\mathrm{et}},\omega_{X,\mathrm{et}})\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(Ra^{\mathrm{Et}}_!M_{\mathrm{et}},A_{n,s}).$$
Taking derived global sections is legitimate on these bounded-below objects. The global comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology] transports both sides to pro-etale global sections. On the left, [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] and the compact-support comparison identify the transported object with $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(M,\omega_{X,n})$. On the right, the same site comparison at $s$, the witness from [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison], and the point comparison from Step 3 identify it with $R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(C_n(M),A_n)$. This yields the required isomorphism in $D(A_n)$.

source.place: Second paragraph: finite-level adjunction on derived mapping complexes via prop-asd-internal-adjunction and finite site comparisons.

proof.text: The map just obtained is the stated $\gamma_{n,M}$. By [lem-asd-internal-adjunction-evaluation], the transpose of the ordinary etale adjunction is the composite of the compact-support projection, evaluation, and exceptional counit $Ra^{\mathrm{Et}}_!\omega_{X,\mathrm{et}}\to A_{n,s}$. The projection comparison [lem-pur-projection-comparison-etale-origin] identifies this projection with the pro-etale projection after the fixed compactification. The bounded site-adjunction transpose statement [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose] and the exceptional-transport statement [lem-sf-etale-proetale-exceptional-transport] identify the transported counit with $F_n\omega_{X,n}\to(A_n)_s$. Finally, the evaluation compatibilities in [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] and [lem-coef-finite-point-internal-hom-evaluation], together with [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison], transport the whole composite. Hence the map is exactly the counit-defined transpose in the statement, rather than an unspecified isomorphism.

proof.text: Each comparison used above is natural in the etale-origin witness and in $M$: this is stated for the internal-Hom and dualizing comparisons, compact supports, projection comparison, adjunction transpose, exceptional transport, and the evaluation-defined point map. Their composite is therefore canonical and natural in $M$, and it agrees with the ordinary etale internal exceptional adjunction followed by global sections and the evaluation-defined finite point identification.

title: Finite-level mapping-complex duality
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use ordinary module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites, with completed coefficient sheaf $R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ for $W=X,s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $F_n=Ra_{!,n}$ for compact support using one fixed compactification $a=pj$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and put $\omega_{X,n}=Ra_n^!A_n$ for the finite constructible comparison-class exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. For $n\ge1$ let $M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ be constructible [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] with finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and put $C_n(M)=\Gamma(s,F_nM)$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Global derived mapping complexes mean derived global sections of derived sheaf Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. There is a canonical natural isomorphism in $D(A_n)$
$$\gamma_{n,M}:\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(M,\omega_{X,n})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(C_n(M),A_n).$$
It is the transpose of compact-support projection followed by evaluation and the exceptional counit $F_n\omega_{X,n}\to(A_n)_s$. Under the finite site comparison [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison], it agrees with the ordinary etale internal exceptional adjunction [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] followed by global sections and the evaluation-defined finite point internal-Hom identification [lem-coef-finite-point-internal-hom-evaluation].
